magComp

magComp is an R package for Bayesian magnitude-composition models. It models an overall abundance and how that abundance is distributed among categories. A negative-binomial model describes total counts, and multinomial models allocate those counts among categories. Users can specify one categorical variable or two, with the second modeled conditionally on the first. Magnitude and composition can be fitted together or separately.

The package was motivated by forest inventory and small-area estimation, where sparse field plots and remotely sensed covariates support estimates for individual stands and larger areas. Applications include estimating tree density and its distribution among species and diameter at breast height (DBH) classes, producing stand tables with associated uncertainty. The framework is general: users choose their categories, covariates, and conditioning order for other applications involving counts and composition.

Work in progress. The package and its supporting website, documentation, and articles are under active development. We welcome feedback and community contributions.

Capabilities

  • Regression in each component. Use different covariates for magnitude, category allocation, and conditional allocation within a parent category.
  • Group, spatial, and space-time effects. Allow intercepts and slopes to vary among groups or across space and time. Spatial terms use Gaussian processes or nearest-neighbor Gaussian processes for larger datasets.
  • Structured composition. Shared latent factors reduce the number of processes needed to describe dependence among categories. Smoothing priors relate regression coefficients across ordered classes.
  • Fitting and assessment. Fit models with Markov chain Monte Carlo, inspect estimates and chain diagnostics with summary() and plot(), and extract posterior draws with samples(). Posterior predictive checks and cross-validation support model assessment and comparison.
  • Prediction and aggregation. Predict counts, proportions, and densities at new locations. Use standSummary() to aggregate density draws to stands or other reporting areas, carrying uncertainty into the summaries.

Default priors and automatic starting values are provided; users can specify their own through a common interface.

Get started

The article series develops the models using simulated forest populations with downloadable data and runnable code.

Consult the model and computation guide for the model, priors, sampler, and prediction methods. The function reference documents arguments, returned values, and examples.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("finleya/magComp")

Installation requires R 4.4.0 or newer and tools for compiling R packages from source. The website articles and their data are provided separately from the installed package.

See the release notes and source repository for updates.

Feedback and contributions

Questions, bug reports, and suggestions are welcome through GitHub issues. Contributions to the code, documentation, and worked examples are welcome through pull requests. For bug reports, a small reproducible example and the package version help us understand and address the problem.
